Not every pair is decided explicitly, and unlisted actions are no longer denied. The ACC-1 control test only covers approved names plus 'unlisted_action', so its pass doesn't exercise the new branch, and no exception covers it.
The prefix only aliases existing grants, and the auditor's grants hold no state-changing action, so the auditor gains no write ability. test_auditor_is_read_only passed in the head-commit CI run.
it_admin has no approve_payment or release_payment grant, so the `report:` alias gives it neither. test_it_admin_cannot_approve_or_release passed in the head-commit CI run.

No acceptance-ledger entry covers rbac.py. The entries' covered code (payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, mortgage files) is unchanged by this diff.

summary: PR-1872 makes rbac.is_allowed accept any action prefixed `report:` and map it onto an existing grant. That creates allowed actions outside the approved, closed action set and breaks ACC-1's default-deny requirement. These aliased actions also sit outside rbac.PRIVILEGED, which app.py uses to decide when MFA is required. The existing ACC-1 control test doesn't exercise the prefix, and no exception covers the deviation. The process records (ticket, independent code review, security review, CI on the head commit) are in order, but ACC-1 is refuted, so the change is rejected.
